subject: Biotechnology
title: Checkpoint Inhibitors
description: A quick win: understand Checkpoint Inhibitors.

hook.text: Cancer hides from your immune system by pressing the brakes — checkpoint inhibitors release those brakes.

buildup.text: PD-1 on T cells acts as an off switch — cancer cells display PD-L1 to silence the attack.

discovery.text: Pembrolizumab blocks PD-1 — T cells wake up and attack tumors they previously ignored.

twist.text: Not all cancers respond — only tumors with many mutations tend to benefit from checkpoint therapy.

climax.text: James Allison and Tasuku Honjo won the 2018 Nobel Prize — their discovery launched modern immunotherapy.

punchline.text: Release the brakes on immunity — and let your body fight the cancer.

quiz.question: How does PD-L1 on cancer cells help tumors evade the immune system?
options: It makes cancer cells invisible to all immune cells
It binds PD-1 on T cells, sending an off signal that prevents attack
It directly kills T cells that approach the tumor

details.summary: Checkpoint inhibitors are antibodies that block immune checkpoints like PD-1 and CTLA-4, releasing the brakes on T cells so they can attack cancer. They have transformed treatment of melanoma, lung cancer, and other malignancies, earning a Nobel Prize in 2018.
details.whyItMatters: Checkpoint inhibitors have produced durable responses in cancers that were previously untreatable, with some patients cancer-free years after treatment. They proved that unleashing the immune system is a viable cancer treatment strategy.
takeaways: Checkpoint inhibitors release immune system brakes to fight cancer
PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade earned the 2018 Nobel Prize in Medicine
They produce durable long-term responses in subset of cancer patients

faq.question: Why do checkpoint inhibitors only work for some cancer patients?
faq.answer: Response depends on tumor mutational burden, PD-L1 expression, immune cell infiltration, and microbiome composition. Tumors with more mutations create more neoantigens for immune recognition. Predicting response remains challenging, and biomarker development is an active research area.

faq.question: What are the side effects of checkpoint inhibitors?
faq.answer: By removing immune brakes, checkpoint inhibitors can cause autoimmune-like reactions affecting any organ. Common immune-related adverse events include colitis, hepatitis, thyroiditis, and skin rashes. Most are manageable with steroids but can occasionally be severe or fatal.
